BiblicalUsage: Pequddah is visitation — God's oversight, and God's reckoning. Eleazar's office was the oversight of all the tabernacle, and Jeremiah says the idols are vanity, and in the time of their visitation they shall perish. Ezekiel heard the cry to call those with charge over the city, and Hosea says the days of visitation are come, the days of recompense are come.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe visitation is both care and judgment: God visits His tabernacle to keep it, and He visits the idols to destroy them. I hold that the same word covers both — He oversees what He loves and reckons with what He hates. The days of visitation always come, and I would rather be visited in mercy than in recompense.
